scenes.heading: Structured Streaming
scenes.narration: Let's take a deep look at Structured Streaming and how it works under the hood in Spark.

scenes.heading: Core model
items: Treats a stream as an unbounded table
scenes.narration: Structured Streaming lets you process live data using the same DataFrame and SQL API you use for batch. Conceptually, it models an incoming stream as a table that grows without bound, and each query result is continuously updated as new rows arrive. Under the hood it runs as a series of small micro-batches, or optionally in a low-latency continuous mode.

scenes.heading: Micro-batch lifecycle
scenes.narration: Each micro-batch begins by reading a new range of data from the source, such as Kafka offsets or newly arrived files. Spark runs the query incrementally over that batch, updating any stateful aggregations it maintains. It then writes the results to the sink and records progress in the checkpoint. This offset-and-checkpoint discipline is what gives streaming its fault tolerance.

scenes.code:
lines = (spark.readStream.format("kafka")
            .option("subscribe", "events").load())
counts = (lines.selectExpr("CAST(value AS STRING) v")
               .groupBy("v").count())
q = (counts.writeStream.outputMode("complete")
           .option("checkpointLocation", "/chk/counts")
           .format("console").start())
q.awaitTermination()
scenes.heading: A minimal streaming query
scenes.narration: This query reads from a Kafka topic as a streaming source and runs a running word count. The readStream and writeStream calls mirror their batch equivalents, which is the whole point of the unified API. The output mode governs how results are emitted, and the checkpoint location is mandatory for recovery. Calling start launches the continuous micro-batch loop.

scenes.heading: Output modes
scenes.narration: Append mode emits only brand-new rows and suits queries without aggregation, or windowed aggregates bounded by a watermark. Complete mode rewrites the entire result table every batch, which fits small aggregations. Update mode emits just the rows whose values changed, a middle ground for incremental aggregations. Choosing the right mode depends on whether and how your query aggregates.

scenes.heading: Delivery & fault tolerance
scenes.narration: Streaming's reliability rests on the checkpoint working with a replayable source and an idempotent sink. On failure, Spark rereads uncommitted offsets from the source and re-applies them, and because the sink is idempotent, no duplicates appear. This combination is what delivers end-to-end exactly-once processing.

scenes.text: Same API, different runtime: batch logic that runs forever.
scenes.narration: Because streaming reuses the batch API, you can prototype logic in batch and productionize it as a stream with minimal changes. Just remember the checkpoint is what makes it recoverable.
